thesis.coreBelief: GD compounds to $435+ over 36 months as the Virginia/Columbia-class delivery ramp and Electric Boat margin inflection drive double-digit EPS growth from a $16.85 2026 base, with the market re-rating the defense shipbuilding franchise from ~22x to ~25x forward earnings on record $136.5B backlog visibility through 2042.
keyAssumptions: Electric Boat maintains or improves the 7.3% Marine operating margin through H2 2026 and into 2027 as workforce efficiency gains compound on the Columbia/Virginia ramp

U.S. Navy submarine procurement funding remains intact in FY2027 appropriations, consistent with the pattern of Congressional add-backs (e.g., $1.9B Virginia-class add in 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act)
invalidationConds: Marine Systems operating margin declines sequentially for two consecutive quarters, signaling Electric Boat execution is deteriorating rather than inflecting
Management delivers two consecutive quarterly EPS misses and cuts full-year guidance, indicating the $136.5B backlog is converting slower than modeled
Congressional action reduces Virginia-class or Columbia-class annual procurement quantities by more than one hull per cycle
thesis.variantView: Consensus treats GD as a slow-growth defense stalwart; I think the multi-decade submarine backlog ($130B total, submarine-heavy) represents a demand floor that makes EPS acceleration over 2027-2029 materially above consensus as Electric Boat ramp rates improve.

triggers.rationale: The old $342 pullback zone has been lost. A review at $315 would represent a fresh leg lower closer to the 52-week low and is now the meaningful downside wake.
A Q2 2026 EPS beat of 3%+ would confirm the Electric Boat margin recovery thesis. Review to consider entering if still watching.
Any earnings miss warrants a review to assess whether it reflects Electric Boat cost overruns, Gulfstream demand weakness, or only delivery timing.
Look at this every 30 days, counting from the last real review.
Buy only when GD reclaims the 50-day average, which would show the pullback has ended and the market is again underwriting the submarine-margin inflection story.

thesis.coreBelief: ISRG compounds to $530+ within 24 months as da Vinci 5 upgrade cycle drives installed-base expansion and instruments/accessories revenue sustains 15%+ growth, materially outpacing any near-term share erosion from JNJ Ottava.
keyAssumptions: da Vinci 5 placements continue at 200+ units/quarter, expanding installed base toward 13,000+ systems by end of 2027 and sustaining 15%+ instruments/accessories revenue growth

JNJ Ottava adoption remains slow and phased due to limited initial indications, retraining requirements, and unknown per-procedure economics — ISRG maintains 70%+ share of robotic soft-tissue procedures through 2027
Aging-population tailwind sustains procedural volume growth at 13%–16% annually as minimally invasive surgery penetration rises in general surgery, urology, and gynecology
ISRG's adjusted gross margin trajectory continues toward 69%+ as da Vinci 5 mix improves and recurring revenue scales
invalidationConds: Procedure volume growth falls below 10% for two consecutive quarters, signaling structural demand erosion rather than cyclical softness
JNJ Ottava captures measurable share in a flagship category (prostatectomy, hysterectomy, or colorectal), defined as 10%+ of new placements in any single quarter
ISRG cuts full-year procedure growth guidance below 12% on two consecutive guidance updates
Adjusted gross margin declines year-over-year, indicating pricing pressure from competitive entrants
CFO or CEO departure combined with a change in capital-allocation priorities (e.g., large dilutive acquisition)
thesis.variantView: Consensus prices in Ottava as a structural threat; ISRG's 11,710-system installed base, 15,000+ da Vinci 5 trained surgeons, and 85% recurring revenue make the moat more durable than feared — the dV5 upgrade cycle is a multi-year earnings driver the market is discounting.

triggers.rationale: Review whether earnings strength confirms da Vinci 5 placements, procedure growth, and margin trajectory.
Review whether an earnings miss reflects temporary noise or a real break in procedure growth, margins, or placements.
